legend.summary: NASA's model of the ocean surface from March 2007 to March 2008: its currents, drawn as flow lines coloured by temperature. A level scan line moves down the map, from the Arctic to Antarctica, once for each quarter of the year.
legend.method: On this track the scan line lies on its side: it runs from west to east and moves from north to south. So here your left ear is west and your right ear is east. The colour of every current is read back to degrees Celsius on NASA's own key, from 0 to 32. Each sweep takes about 16 seconds.

items.meaning: Sea under the scan line. It is there over any water, alone over cold seas, and almost silent where the line crosses only land or ice. It is louder when more of the line is sea.

Warm water under the line. The warmer it is, the more voices join on top, each one higher: a fifth from 6 degrees, more voices from 12, 18 and 24 degrees, and the highest from 28 degrees, the warmest seas on Earth.
Where along the line the warm water is: each voice leans toward it, west in your left ear, east in your right ear.

legend.caveat: Temperatures are read from the colours of NASA's flow lines, so they are the model's sea surface temperature as NASA drew it, to about one degree, and only where a current is drawn: land, sea ice and Antarctica have no reading. NASA's key starts at 0 degrees, so colder water near the ice reads as 0 to 2 degrees. Each sweep is one quarter of NASA's year-long movie, the middle value of every reading in it, so short changes inside a quarter are smoothed away.
